latin: Aeneadum genetrix, hominum divomque voluptas,
en: Mother of Aeneas' race, pleasure of men and gods,

latin: alma Venus, caeli subter labentia signa
en: nourishing Venus, who beneath the gliding signs of heaven

latin: quae mare navigerum, quae terras frugiferentis
en: fill with life the ship-bearing sea, the grain-bearing lands,

latin: concelebras, per te quoniam genus omne animantum
en: and throng them, since through you every kind of living thing

latin: concipitur visitque exortum lumina solis:
en: is conceived and, risen, looks upon the light of the sun:

latin: te, dea, te fugiunt venti, te nubila caeli
en: you, goddess, you the winds flee, you the clouds of heaven flee,

latin: adventumque tuum, tibi suavis daedala tellus
en: you and your coming; for you the artificer earth sends up

latin: summittit flores, tibi rident aequora ponti
en: her sweet flowers, for you the levels of the sea laugh,

latin: placatumque nitet diffuso lumine caelum.
en: and the sky, made calm, shines with light poured wide.

latin: nam simul ac species patefactast verna diei
en: For as soon as the face of the spring day stands revealed

latin: et reserata viget genitabilis aura favoni,
en: and the fertile breath of the west wind, unbarred, grows strong,

latin: aeriae primum volucris te, diva, tuumque
en: first the birds of the air, goddess, announce you and your

latin: significant initum perculsae corda tua vi.
en: coming in, their hearts struck through by your power.

latin: inde ferae pecudes persultant pabula laeta
en: Then wild beasts and herds go bounding over the glad pastures

latin: et rapidos tranant amnis: ita capta lepore
en: and swim the rushing rivers: so, captured by your charm,

latin: te sequitur cupide quo quamque inducere pergis.
en: each follows you eagerly wherever you go on to lead.

latin: denique per maria ac montis fluviosque rapacis
en: Then through seas and mountains and sweeping rivers,

latin: frondiferasque domos avium camposque virentis
en: through the leafy homes of birds and the greening plains,

latin: omnibus incutiens blandum per pectora amorem
en: striking seductive love into the breasts of all,

latin: efficis ut cupide generatim saecla propagent.
en: you make them eagerly propagate their generations, kind by kind.

latin: quae quoniam rerum naturam sola gubernas
en: Since you alone steer the nature of things,

latin: nec sine te quicquam dias in luminis oras
en: and without you nothing rises into the shining shores of light,

latin: exoritur neque fit laetum neque amabile quicquam,
en: and nothing comes to be glad, nothing lovely,

latin: te sociam studeo scribendis versibus esse,
en: I long for you as my partner in writing these verses

latin: quos ego de rerum natura pangere conor
en: which I attempt to set down on the nature of things

latin: Memmiadae nostro, quem tu, dea, tempore in omni
en: for our son of the Memmii, whom you, goddess, at every season

latin: omnibus ornatum voluisti excellere rebus.
en: have willed to excel, adorned with every gift.

latin: quo magis aeternum da dictis, diva, leporem.
en: All the more, goddess, give my words a lasting charm.

latin: effice ut interea fera moenera militiai
en: Bring it about that meanwhile the savage works of war

latin: per maria ac terras omnis sopita quiescant;
en: over all seas and lands be lulled and lie at rest;

latin: nam tu sola potes tranquilla pace iuvare
en: for you alone can help mortals with tranquil peace,

latin: mortalis, quoniam belli fera moenera Mavors
en: since Mars, mighty in arms, who rules the savage works

latin: armipotens regit, in gremium qui saepe tuum se
en: of war, often throws himself back into your lap,

latin: reiicit aeterno devictus vulnere amoris,
en: conquered by the eternal wound of love,

latin: atque ita suspiciens tereti cervice reposta
en: and so, gazing up, his rounded neck laid back,

latin: pascit amore avidos inhians in te, dea, visus
en: feeds on love his hungry eyes, gaping at you, goddess,

latin: eque tuo pendet resupini spiritus ore.
en: and the breath of him, reclining, hangs upon your lips.

latin: hunc tu, diva, tuo recubantem corpore sancto
en: Goddess, as he lies back upon your holy body,

latin: circum fusa super, suavis ex ore loquellas
en: pour yourself around and over him, and from your lips

latin: funde petens placidam Romanis, incluta, pacem;
en: pour out sweet speech, asking calm peace, glorious one, for the Romans;

latin: nam neque nos agere hoc patriai tempore iniquo
en: for neither can we, in a bad time for our country, do this work

latin: possumus aequo animo nec Memmi clara propago
en: with an untroubled mind, nor can the famous offspring of Memmius

latin: talibus in rebus communi desse saluti.
en: in such a pass be wanting to the common safety.

latin: omnis enim per se divum natura necessest
en: For the whole nature of the gods must, of itself, by necessity

latin: immortali aevo summa cum pace fruatur
en: enjoy immortal life in utmost peace,

latin: semota ab nostris rebus seiunctaque longe;
en: removed from our affairs and separated far away;

latin: nam privata dolore omni, privata periclis,
en: for free from every pain, free from dangers,

latin: ipsa suis pollens opibus, nihil indiga nostri,
en: strong in its own resources, needing nothing of ours,

latin: nec bene promeritis capitur nec tangitur ira.
en: it is neither won by services nor touched by anger.

latin: Quod super est, vacuas auris animumque sagacem
en: For the rest, lend ears set free, and a keen mind

latin: semotum a curis adhibe veram ad rationem,
en: withdrawn from cares, to true reasoning,

latin: ne mea dona tibi studio disposta fideli,
en: so that my gifts, laid out for you with faithful care,

latin: intellecta prius quam sint, contempta relinquas.
en: you do not, before they are understood, scorn and leave behind.

latin: nam tibi de summa caeli ratione deumque
en: For I shall begin to set out for you the highest order

latin: disserere incipiam et rerum primordia pandam,
en: of heaven and the gods, and unfold the first-beginnings of things,

latin: unde omnis natura creet res, auctet alatque,
en: from which nature creates all things, makes them grow, and feeds them,

latin: quove eadem rursum natura perempta resolvat,
en: and into which, when they perish, that same nature dissolves them,

latin: quae nos materiem et genitalia corpora rebus
en: which we, in giving our account, are used to calling matter

latin: reddunda in ratione vocare et semina rerum
en: and the generative bodies of things, and to name

latin: appellare suemus et haec eadem usurpare
en: seeds of things, and to use for these same things the term

latin: corpora prima, quod ex illis sunt omnia primis.
en: first bodies, because from them, as first, all things are.

latin: Humana ante oculos foede cum vita iaceret
en: When human life lay foully before the eyes,

latin: in terris oppressa gravi sub religione,
en: crushed on the earth beneath the weight of religion,

latin: quae caput a caeli regionibus ostendebat
en: which showed its head from the regions of heaven,

latin: horribili super aspectu mortalibus instans,
en: looming over mortals with horrible aspect,

latin: primum Graius homo mortalis tollere contra
en: first a man of Greece dared to lift mortal eyes

latin: est oculos ausus primusque obsistere contra;
en: against it, and first to take a stand against it;

latin: quem neque fama deum nec fulmina nec minitanti
en: him neither the fame of gods nor thunderbolts nor heaven

latin: murmure compressit caelum, sed eo magis acrem
en: with its threatening growl held down; rather they goaded

latin: inritat animi virtutem, effringere ut arta
en: the keen courage of his mind the more, so that he longed

latin: naturae primus portarum claustra cupiret.
en: to be first to break the tight-barred gates of nature.

latin: ergo vivida vis animi pervicit et extra
en: And so the living force of his mind prevailed, and far

latin: processit longe flammantia moenia mundi
en: beyond the flaming walls of the world he went out

latin: atque omne immensum peragravit mente animoque,
en: and traveled the whole immensity in thought and mind,

latin: unde refert nobis victor quid possit oriri,
en: from where he brings back to us, a victor, what can come to be

latin: quid nequeat, finita potestas denique cuique
en: and what cannot, and how at last each thing's power is bounded,

latin: qua nam sit ratione atque alte terminus haerens.
en: by what principle, and its boundary-stone set deep.

latin: quare religio pedibus subiecta vicissim
en: Therefore religion in its turn is thrown beneath our feet

latin: opteritur, nos exaequat victoria caelo.
en: and trampled; the victory lifts us level with heaven.

latin: Illud in his rebus vereor, ne forte rearis
en: In these matters I fear this: that you might think

latin: impia te rationis inire elementa viamque
en: you enter on the impious elements of reasoning and set foot

latin: indugredi sceleris. quod contra saepius illa
en: on the road of crime. Rather, the opposite: more often it is

latin: religio peperit scelerosa atque impia facta.
en: religion that has borne the criminal and impious deeds.

latin: Aulide quo pacto Triviai virginis aram
en: As at Aulis, where the altar of the Virgin of the Crossways

latin: Iphianassai turparunt sanguine foede
en: was foully defiled with the blood of Iphianassa

latin: ductores Danaum delecti, prima virorum.
en: by the chosen leaders of the Danaans, the first of men.

latin: cui simul infula virgineos circum data comptus
en: As soon as the ribbon, bound about her maiden hair,

latin: ex utraque pari malarum parte profusast,
en: streamed down in equal lengths on either cheek,

latin: et maestum simul ante aras adstare parentem
en: and she saw her father standing sorrowful before the altar,

latin: sensit et hunc propter ferrum celare ministros
en: and beside him the attendants hiding the knife,

latin: aspectuque suo lacrimas effundere civis,
en: and the citizens shedding tears at the sight of her,

latin: muta metu terram genibus summissa petebat.
en: mute with fear, her knees giving way, she sank to the ground.

latin: nec miserae prodesse in tali tempore quibat,
en: Nor could it help the poor girl at such a moment

latin: quod patrio princeps donarat nomine regem;
en: that she had been the first to give the king the name of father;

latin: nam sublata virum manibus tremibundaque ad aras
en: for lifted by men's hands and trembling she was led

latin: deductast, non ut sollemni more sacrorum
en: to the altar, not so that, when the solemn rite was done,

latin: perfecto posset claro comitari Hymenaeo,
en: she might be escorted by the ringing wedding-hymn,

latin: sed casta inceste nubendi tempore in ipso
en: but so that, pure, impurely, at the very season of marriage,

latin: hostia concideret mactatu maesta parentis,
en: she might fall, a grieving victim, slaughtered by her father,

latin: exitus ut classi felix faustusque daretur.
en: that a happy and favorable departure be granted the fleet.

latin: tantum religio potuit suadere malorum.
en: So much evil could religion prompt.

latin: Tutemet a nobis iam quovis tempore vatum
en: You yourself, at any moment now, overcome by the prophets'

latin: terriloquis victus dictis desciscere quaeres.
en: terror-speaking words, will look to desert us.

latin: quippe etenim quam multa tibi iam fingere possunt
en: For indeed how many dreams they can even now invent for you,

latin: somnia, quae vitae rationes vertere possint
en: dreams that could overturn the reasonings of your life

latin: fortunasque tuas omnis turbare timore!
en: and trouble all your fortunes with fear!

latin: et merito; nam si certam finem esse viderent
en: And with reason: for if men saw a sure end

latin: aerumnarum homines, aliqua ratione valerent
en: to their troubles, they would by some means find strength

latin: religionibus atque minis obsistere vatum.
en: to stand against the religions and the threats of prophets.

latin: nunc ratio nulla est restandi, nulla facultas,
en: As it is, there is no way to stand against them, no power,

latin: aeternas quoniam poenas in morte timendum.
en: since eternal punishments must be feared in death.

latin: ignoratur enim quae sit natura animai,
en: For it is not known what the nature of the spirit is,

latin: nata sit an contra nascentibus insinuetur
en: whether it is born, or instead works its way into us at birth,

latin: et simul intereat nobiscum morte dirempta
en: and whether it perishes together with us, torn apart by death,

latin: an tenebras Orci visat vastasque lacunas
en: or visits the darkness of Orcus and his vast pools,

latin: an pecudes alias divinitus insinuet se,
en: or by divine ordinance slips itself into other beasts,

latin: Ennius ut noster cecinit, qui primus amoeno
en: as our Ennius sang, who first brought down

latin: detulit ex Helicone perenni fronde coronam,
en: from lovely Helicon a crown of unfading leaf

latin: per gentis Italas hominum quae clara clueret;
en: to shine in fame through the Italian nations of men;

latin: etsi praeterea tamen esse Acherusia templa
en: and yet besides, that the precincts of Acheron exist

latin: Ennius aeternis exponit versibus edens,
en: Ennius sets forth, declaring it in eternal verses,

latin: quo neque permaneant animae neque corpora nostra,
en: where neither our spirits nor our bodies endure,

latin: sed quaedam simulacra modis pallentia miris;
en: but certain images, pale in strange ways;

latin: unde sibi exortam semper florentis Homeri
en: from there, he recalls, the likeness of ever-flourishing Homer

latin: commemorat speciem lacrimas effundere salsas
en: rose up before him and began to shed salt tears

latin: coepisse et rerum naturam expandere dictis.
en: and to unfold in words the nature of things.

latin: qua propter bene cum superis de rebus habenda
en: Therefore, while we must give a good account of things

latin: nobis est ratio, solis lunaeque meatus
en: above, by what principle the courses of sun and moon

latin: qua fiant ratione, et qua vi quaeque gerantur
en: come about, and by what force each thing is carried on

latin: in terris, tunc cum primis ratione sagaci
en: upon the earth, then above all with keen reasoning

latin: unde anima atque animi constet natura videndum,
en: we must see of what the spirit and the nature of the mind consist,

latin: et quae res nobis vigilantibus obvia mentes
en: and what thing it is that meets us and terrifies our minds

latin: terrificet morbo adfectis somnoque sepultis,
en: when we are awake but stricken with sickness, or buried in sleep,

latin: cernere uti videamur eos audireque coram,
en: so that we seem to see and hear face to face

latin: morte obita quorum tellus amplectitur ossa.
en: those whose bones, after death, the earth embraces.

latin: Nec me animi fallit Graiorum obscura reperta
en: Nor does it escape my mind that the obscure findings of the Greeks

latin: difficile inlustrare Latinis versibus esse,
en: are hard to set in light in Latin verses,

latin: multa novis verbis praesertim cum sit agendum
en: especially since much must be done with new words

latin: propter egestatem linguae et rerum novitatem;
en: because of the poverty of the language and the newness of the things;

latin: sed tua me virtus tamen et sperata voluptas
en: but still your worth, and the hoped-for pleasure

latin: suavis amicitiae quemvis efferre laborem
en: of sweet friendship, urge me to bear any labor,

latin: suadet et inducit noctes vigilare serenas
en: and lead me to keep watch through the calm nights,

latin: quaerentem dictis quibus et quo carmine demum
en: searching with what words and with what song at last

latin: clara tuae possim praepandere lumina menti,
en: I may spread clear lights before your mind

latin: res quibus occultas penitus convisere possis.
en: by which you can see deep into hidden things.

latin: hunc igitur terrorem animi tenebrasque necessest
en: This terror of the mind, then, and this darkness

latin: non radii solis neque lucida tela diei
en: must be scattered not by the sun's rays or the bright shafts of day

latin: discutiant, sed naturae species ratioque.
en: but by the face and reasoning of nature.

latin: Principium cuius hinc nobis exordia sumet,
en: Its first principle will take its starting-point for us from here:

latin: nullam rem e nihilo gigni divinitus umquam.
en: that nothing is ever begotten from nothing by divine will.

latin: quippe ita formido mortalis continet omnis,
en: Indeed, fear so holds all mortals in its grip

latin: quod multa in terris fieri caeloque tuentur,
en: because they behold many things happening on earth and in the sky

latin: quorum operum causas nulla ratione videre
en: the causes of whose workings they can in no way see,

latin: possunt ac fieri divino numine rentur.
en: and they suppose them to be done by divine power.

latin: quas ob res ubi viderimus nil posse creari
en: For these reasons, when we have seen that nothing can be created

latin: de nihilo, tum quod sequimur iam rectius inde
en: from nothing, then we shall more rightly discern from there

latin: perspiciemus, et unde queat res quaeque creari
en: what we are seeking: both from what each thing can be created

latin: et quo quaeque modo fiant opera sine divom.
en: and in what manner all things come about without the labor of gods.

latin: Nam si de nihilo fierent, ex omnibus rebus
en: For if things came to be from nothing, out of all things

latin: omne genus nasci posset, nil semine egeret.
en: every kind could be born; nothing would need a seed.

latin: e mare primum homines, e terra posset oriri
en: First, men could rise out of the sea, and out of the earth

latin: squamigerum genus et volucres erumpere caelo;
en: the scaly race, and birds could burst out of the sky;

latin: armenta atque aliae pecudes, genus omne ferarum,
en: herds and other cattle, every kind of wild beast,

latin: incerto partu culta ac deserta tenerent.
en: born at random, would occupy the tilled land and the wild.

latin: nec fructus idem arboribus constare solerent,
en: Nor would the same fruits stay constant on the trees,

latin: sed mutarentur, ferre omnes omnia possent.
en: but would change; all trees could bear all fruits.

latin: quippe ubi non essent genitalia corpora cuique,
en: For where there were no generative bodies for each thing,

latin: qui posset mater rebus consistere certa?
en: how could there be a fixed mother for things?

latin: at nunc seminibus quia certis quaeque creantur,
en: But as it is, since each thing is created from fixed seeds,

latin: inde enascitur atque oras in luminis exit,
en: it is born and comes forth into the shores of light

latin: materies ubi inest cuiusque et corpora prima;
en: from that place where the matter of each and its first bodies are;

latin: atque hac re nequeunt ex omnibus omnia gigni,
en: and for this reason all things cannot be begotten from all,

latin: quod certis in rebus inest secreta facultas.
en: because in fixed things there dwells a separate power.

latin: Praeterea cur vere rosam, frumenta calore,
en: Further, why do we see the rose poured forth in spring, grain in the heat,

latin: vites autumno fundi suadente videmus,
en: vines when autumn urges them on,

latin: si non, certa suo quia tempore semina rerum
en: if not because, when fixed seeds of things at their own time

latin: cum confluxerunt, patefit quod cumque creatur,
en: have flowed together, whatever is created is disclosed

latin: dum tempestates adsunt et vivida tellus
en: while the seasons are at hand, and the living earth

latin: tuto res teneras effert in luminis oras?
en: brings tender things safely forth into the shores of light?

latin: quod si de nihilo fierent, subito exorerentur
en: But if they came from nothing, they would spring up suddenly

latin: incerto spatio atque alienis partibus anni,
en: at uncertain intervals and in alien parts of the year,

latin: quippe ubi nulla forent primordia, quae genitali
en: since there would be no first-beginnings that could be kept

latin: concilio possent arceri tempore iniquo.
en: from generative union by an unfavorable season.

latin: Nec porro augendis rebus spatio foret usus
en: Nor again, for things to grow, would there be need of time

latin: seminis ad coitum, si e nilo crescere possent;
en: for the meeting of seed, if they could grow out of nothing;

latin: nam fierent iuvenes subito ex infantibus parvis
en: for little infants would suddenly become young men,

latin: e terraque exorta repente arbusta salirent.
en: and trees, risen from the earth, would leap up all at once.

latin: quorum nil fieri manifestum est, omnia quando
en: It is plain that none of this happens, since all things

latin: paulatim crescunt, ut par est semine certo,
en: grow little by little, as is fitting, from fixed seed,

latin: crescentesque genus servant; ut noscere possis
en: and as they grow they keep their kind; so that you can know

latin: quicque sua de materia grandescere alique.
en: that each thing grows large and is nourished from its own matter.

latin: Huc accedit uti sine certis imbribus anni
en: To this is added that without the year's fixed rains

latin: laetificos nequeat fetus submittere tellus
en: the earth could not send up its gladdening produce,

latin: nec porro secreta cibo natura animantum
en: nor again could the nature of living things, kept apart from food,

latin: propagare genus possit vitamque tueri;
en: propagate its kind and preserve its life;

latin: ut potius multis communia corpora rebus
en: so that you should rather think that many bodies are common

latin: multa putes esse, ut verbis elementa videmus,
en: to many things, as we see elements are to words,

latin: quam sine principiis ullam rem existere posse.
en: than that anything could exist without beginnings.

latin: Denique cur homines tantos natura parare
en: Again, why could nature not produce men so huge

latin: non potuit, pedibus qui pontum per vada possent
en: that they could cross the sea on foot, wading through its shallows,

latin: transire et magnos manibus divellere montis
en: and tear great mountains apart with their hands,

latin: multaque vivendo vitalia vincere saecla,
en: and in living outlast many generations of the living,

latin: si non, materies quia rebus reddita certast
en: if not because fixed matter has been assigned to things

latin: gignundis, e qua constat quid possit oriri?
en: for their begetting, from which it stands what can arise?

latin: nil igitur fieri de nilo posse fatendumst,
en: Therefore it must be confessed that nothing can come from nothing,

latin: semine quando opus est rebus, quo quaeque creatae
en: since things need seed, from which each, once created,

latin: aeris in teneras possint proferrier auras.
en: can be brought forth into the tender breezes of the air.

latin: Postremo quoniam incultis praestare videmus
en: Finally, since we see that tilled places surpass

latin: culta loca et manibus melioris reddere fetus,
en: the untilled, and yield better produce to our hands,

latin: esse videlicet in terris primordia rerum
en: there are, it is clear, first-beginnings of things in the earth

latin: quae nos fecundas vertentes vomere glebas
en: which we, turning the fertile clods with the plowshare

latin: terraique solum subigentes cimus ad ortus;
en: and working the soil of the earth, rouse to birth;

latin: quod si nulla forent, nostro sine quaeque labore
en: but if there were none, you would see each thing, without our labor,

latin: sponte sua multo fieri meliora videres.
en: come of its own accord to be much better.

latin: Huc accedit uti quicque in sua corpora rursum
en: To this is added that nature dissolves each thing back

latin: dissoluat natura neque ad nihilum interemat res.
en: into its own bodies, and does not destroy things into nothing.

latin: nam siquid mortale e cunctis partibus esset,
en: For if anything were mortal in all its parts,

latin: ex oculis res quaeque repente erepta periret;
en: each thing would suddenly perish, snatched from our eyes;

latin: nulla vi foret usus enim, quae partibus eius
en: for there would be no need of any force that could bring about

latin: discidium parere et nexus exsolvere posset.
en: division among its parts and undo their bonds.

latin: quod nunc, aeterno quia constant semine quaeque,
en: As it is, since each thing is made of eternal seed,

latin: donec vis obiit, quae res diverberet ictu
en: until a force has met it that can shatter things with a blow

latin: aut intus penetret per inania dissoluatque,
en: or pierce within through the voids and dissolve them,

latin: nullius exitium patitur natura videri.
en: nature does not allow the destruction of anything to be seen.

latin: Praeterea quae cumque vetustate amovet aetas,
en: Further, whatever things time removes through age,

latin: si penitus peremit consumens materiem omnem,
en: if it destroys them utterly, consuming all their matter,

latin: unde animale genus generatim in lumina vitae
en: from where does Venus lead the race of living things, kind by kind,

latin: redducit Venus, aut redductum daedala tellus
en: back into the light of life? Or, once led back, from where does the artificer earth

latin: unde alit atque auget generatim pabula praebens?
en: nourish and increase them, kind by kind, providing food?

latin: unde mare ingenuei fontes externaque longe
en: From where do native springs and rivers from far outside

latin: flumina suppeditant? unde aether sidera pascit?
en: keep the sea supplied? From where does the ether feed the stars?

latin: tum quae res instet, quid porro deinde sequatur;
en: then what thing is at hand, and what will follow after;

latin: nec per se quemquam tempus sentire fatendumst
en: nor must it be admitted that anyone senses time by itself,

latin: semotum ab rerum motu placidaque quiete.
en: apart from the motion of things and their calm rest.

latin: denique Tyndaridem raptam belloque subactas
en: Finally, when they say the abduction of Tyndareus' daughter

latin: Troiiugenas gentis cum dicunt esse, videndumst
en: and the conquest of the Trojan-born nations in war "are", we must take care

latin: ne forte haec per se cogant nos esse fateri,
en: that they do not force us to admit these things exist by themselves,

latin: quando ea saecla hominum, quorum haec eventa fuerunt,
en: since the generations of men whose accidents these were

latin: inrevocabilis abstulerit iam praeterita aetas;
en: have been carried off already by an age gone past recall;

latin: namque aliud terris, aliud regionibus ipsis
en: for one thing will be said to be an accident of the lands, another

latin: eventum dici poterit quod cumque erit actum.
en: of the regions themselves, whatever has been done.

latin: denique materies si rerum nulla fuisset
en: Finally, if there had been no matter of things,

latin: nec locus ac spatium, res in quo quaeque geruntur,
en: and no place and space, in which each thing is carried on,

latin: numquam Tyndaridis forma conflatus amore
en: never would the fire, kindled by love for the beauty of Tyndareus' daughter,

latin: ignis Alexandri Phrygio sub pectore gliscens
en: glowing beneath the Phrygian breast of Alexander,

latin: clara accendisset saevi certamina belli
en: have lit the famous contests of savage war,

latin: nec clam durateus Troiianis Pergama partu
en: nor would the wooden horse, unknown to the Trojans, have set Pergamum

latin: inflammasset equos nocturno Graiiugenarum;
en: ablaze by its night-time delivery of the sons of the Greeks;

latin: perspicere ut possis res gestas funditus omnis
en: so that you may see clearly that all deeds done, from the ground up,

latin: non ita uti corpus per se constare neque esse
en: do not exist or have being by themselves as body does,

latin: nec ratione cluere eadem qua constet inane,
en: nor are spoken of on the same principle as void,

latin: sed magis ut merito possis eventa vocare
en: but rather that you may justly call them accidents

latin: corporis atque loci, res in quo quaeque gerantur.
en: of body and of place, in which each thing is carried on.

latin: Corpora sunt porro partim primordia rerum,
en: Further, bodies are partly the first-beginnings of things,

latin: partim concilio quae constant principiorum.
en: partly those that are formed from a union of beginnings.

latin: sed quae sunt rerum primordia, nulla potest vis
en: But those that are the first-beginnings of things no force

latin: stinguere; nam solido vincunt ea corpore demum.
en: can quench; for it is by solid body that they prevail.

latin: etsi difficile esse videtur credere quicquam
en: And yet it seems hard to believe that anything

latin: in rebus solido reperiri corpore posse.
en: among things can be found to be of solid body.

latin: transit enim fulmen caeli per saepta domorum
en: For the thunderbolt of heaven passes through the walls of houses,

latin: clamor ut ac voces, ferrum candescit in igni
en: as do shouting and voices; iron grows white-hot in fire,

latin: dissiliuntque fero ferventi saxa vapore;
en: and rocks leap apart in fierce and seething heat;

latin: cum labefactatus rigor auri solvitur aestu,
en: when the hardness of gold is shaken loose and dissolves in heat,

latin: tum glacies aeris flamma devicta liquescit;
en: then the ice of bronze, conquered by flame, melts away;

latin: permanat calor argentum penetraleque frigus,
en: heat seeps through silver, and so does penetrating cold,

latin: quando utrumque manu retinentes pocula rite
en: since, gripping cups in hand as is the custom, we have felt both

latin: sensimus infuso lympharum rore superne.
en: when the dew of water was poured in from above.

latin: usque adeo in rebus solidi nihil esse videtur.
en: To such a degree there seems to be nothing solid in things.

latin: sed quia vera tamen ratio naturaque rerum
en: But since true reasoning and the nature of things nonetheless

latin: cogit, ades, paucis dum versibus expediamus
en: compel us, attend, while in a few verses we make it plain

latin: esse ea quae solido atque aeterno corpore constent,
en: that there are things which consist of solid and eternal body,

latin: semina quae rerum primordiaque esse docemus,
en: which we teach are the seeds of things and their first-beginnings,

latin: unde omnis rerum nunc constet summa creata.
en: from which the whole sum of things now stands created.

latin: Principio quoniam duplex natura duarum
en: To begin with, since the twofold nature of two things,

latin: dissimilis rerum longe constare repertast,
en: far unlike each other, has been found to exist,

latin: corporis atque loci, res in quo quaeque geruntur,
en: of body and of place, in which each thing is carried on,

latin: esse utramque sibi per se puramque necessest.
en: each of necessity must exist by itself and pure.

latin: nam qua cumque vacat spatium, quod inane vocamus,
en: For wherever there is empty space, which we call void,

latin: corpus ea non est; qua porro cumque tenet se
en: there body is not; and further, wherever body

latin: corpus, ea vacuum nequaquam constat inane.
en: holds its place, there empty void by no means exists.

latin: sunt igitur solida ac sine inani corpora prima.
en: The first bodies, therefore, are solid and without void.

latin: Praeterea quoniam genitis in rebus inanest,
en: Further, since there is void in things that have been born,

latin: materiem circum solidam constare necessest;
en: solid matter must stand around it;

latin: nec res ulla potest vera ratione probari
en: nor can anything be proved by true reasoning

latin: corpore inane suo celare atque intus habere,
en: to hide void in its body and to hold it within,

latin: si non, quod cohibet, solidum constare relinquas.
en: unless you grant that what encloses it stands solid.

latin: id porro nihil esse potest nisi materiai
en: And that, further, can be nothing but a union

latin: concilium, quod inane queat rerum cohibere.
en: of matter, such as could enclose the void in things.

latin: materies igitur, solido quae corpore constat,
en: Matter, therefore, which consists of solid body,

latin: esse aeterna potest, cum cetera dissoluantur.
en: can be eternal, while all else is dissolved.

latin: Tum porro si nil esset quod inane vocaret,
en: Then again, if there were nothing that stood empty as void,

latin: omne foret solidum; nisi contra corpora certa
en: all would be solid; unless, on the other hand, there were definite bodies

latin: essent quae loca complerent quae cumque tenerent
en: to fill up whatever places they occupied,

latin: omne quod est spatium, vacuum constaret inane.
en: all the space there is would stand as empty void.

latin: alternis igitur ni mirum corpus inani
en: Body, therefore, is plainly marked off from void

latin: distinctum, quoniam nec plenum naviter extat
en: in alternation, since neither does the wholly full exist

latin: nec porro vacuum; sunt ergo corpora certa,
en: nor, again, the wholly empty; there are, then, definite bodies

latin: quae spatium pleno possint distinguere inane.
en: that can mark off empty space from full.

latin: haec neque dissolui plagis extrinsecus icta
en: These can neither be dissolved when struck by blows from outside

latin: possunt nec porro penitus penetrata retexi
en: nor, again, be unravelled by being pierced to the core,

latin: nec ratione queunt alia temptata labare;
en: nor, assailed in any other way, can they be made to give;

latin: id quod iam supra tibi paulo ostendimus ante.
en: as I showed you above, a little while before.

latin: nam neque conlidi sine inani posse videtur
en: For nothing, it seems, can be crushed without void,

latin: quicquam nec frangi nec findi in bina secando
en: nor broken, nor split in two by cutting,

latin: nec capere umorem neque item manabile frigus
en: nor take in moisture, nor likewise seeping cold,

latin: nec penetralem ignem, quibus omnia conficiuntur.
en: nor penetrating fire, by which all things are undone.

latin: et quo quaeque magis cohibet res intus inane,
en: And the more void each thing holds within it,

latin: tam magis his rebus penitus temptata labascit.
en: the more it gives way when assailed to the core by these.

latin: ergo si solida ac sine inani corpora prima
en: Therefore if the first bodies are solid and without void,

latin: sunt ita uti docui, sint haec aeterna necessest.
en: as I have taught, they must be eternal.

latin: Praeterea nisi materies aeterna fuisset,
en: Further, unless matter had been eternal,

latin: antehac ad nihilum penitus res quaeque redissent
en: before now all things would have gone back utterly to nothing,

latin: de nihiloque renata forent quae cumque videmus.
en: and from nothing would have been reborn whatever we see.

latin: at quoniam supra docui nil posse creari
en: But since I taught above that nothing can be created

latin: de nihilo neque quod genitumst ad nil revocari,
en: from nothing, nor what has been born be called back to nothing,

latin: esse inmortali primordia corpore debent,
en: the first-beginnings must be of immortal body,

latin: dissolui quo quaeque supremo tempore possint,
en: into which all things can be dissolved at their last hour,

latin: materies ut subpeditet rebus reparandis.
en: so that matter may be at hand for the renewal of things.

latin: sunt igitur solida primordia simplicitate
en: The first-beginnings, therefore, are of solid singleness,

latin: nec ratione queunt alia servata per aevom
en: nor in any other way could they have been kept through the ages

latin: ex infinito iam tempore res reparare.
en: to renew things, from time already infinite.

latin: denique si nullam finem natura parasset
en: Finally, if nature had set no limit

latin: frangendis rebus, iam corpora materiai
en: to the breaking of things, by now the bodies of matter

latin: usque redacta forent aevo frangente priore,
en: would have been so worn down by the breaking of past ages

latin: ut nihil ex illis a certo tempore posset
en: that nothing conceived from them, from a fixed time on,

latin: conceptum summum aetatis pervadere finem.
en: could reach the furthest goal of its age.

latin: nam quidvis citius dissolvi posse videmus
en: For we see that anything can be dissolved more quickly

latin: quam rursus refici; qua propter longa diei
en: than made again; therefore whatever the long span of days,

latin: infinita aetas ante acti temporis omnis
en: the infinite age of all the time gone before,

latin: quod fregisset adhuc disturbans dissoluensque,
en: had broken till now, confounding and dissolving it,

latin: numquam relicuo reparari tempore posset.
en: could never be repaired in the time remaining.

latin: at nunc ni mirum frangendi reddita finis
en: But as it is, a fixed limit to breaking, plainly,

latin: certa manet, quoniam refici rem quamque videmus
en: remains assigned, since we see each thing made again,

latin: et finita simul generatim tempora rebus
en: and at the same time fixed seasons, kind by kind, stand set

latin: stare, quibus possint aevi contingere florem.
en: for things, in which they can reach the flower of their age.

latin: Huc accedit uti, solidissima materiai
en: Add to this that, although the bodies of matter

latin: corpora cum constant, possint tamen omnia reddi,
en: are most solid, an account can still be given of all things

latin: mollia quae fiunt, aer aqua terra vapores,
en: that come to be soft, air, water, earth, vapors,

latin: quo pacto fiant et qua vi quaeque gerantur,
en: how they come to be and by what force each is carried on,

latin: admixtum quoniam semel est in rebus inane.
en: since void is mixed, once and for all, in things.

latin: at contra si mollia sint primordia rerum,
en: But if, on the contrary, the first-beginnings of things were soft,

latin: unde queant validi silices ferrumque creari,
en: how hard flints and iron could be created

latin: non poterit ratio reddi; nam funditus omnis
en: no account could be given; for utterly all

latin: principio fundamenti natura carebit.
en: nature will lack a beginning for its foundation.

latin: sunt igitur solida pollentia simplicitate,
en: They are, therefore, strong in solid singleness,

latin: quorum condenso magis omnia conciliatu
en: and by a denser union of them all things

latin: artari possunt validasque ostendere viris.
en: can be packed tight and show forth sturdy strength.

latin: porro si nullast frangendis reddita finis
en: Further, if no limit has been set to the breaking

latin: corporibus, tamen ex aeterno tempore quaeque
en: of bodies, still, out of eternal time, certain bodies

latin: nunc etiam superare necessest corpora rebus,
en: must even now survive in things,

latin: quae non dum clueant ullo temptata periclo.
en: such as have not yet been assailed by any danger.

latin: at quoniam fragili natura praedita constant,
en: But since they are endowed with a fragile nature,

latin: discrepat aeternum tempus potuisse manere
en: it is inconsistent that they could have lasted through eternal time,

latin: innumerabilibus plagis vexata per aevom.
en: harried through the ages by numberless blows.

latin: Denique iam quoniam generatim reddita finis
en: Finally, since a limit is set for things, kind by kind,

latin: crescendi rebus constat vitamque tenendi,
en: to their growing and their holding on to life,

latin: et quid quaeque queant per foedera naturai,
en: and since what each can do by nature's covenants,

latin: quid porro nequeant, sancitum quando quidem extat,
en: and what, further, each cannot, stands decreed,

latin: nec commutatur quicquam, quin omnia constant
en: nor is anything changed, but all things are so constant

latin: usque adeo, variae volucres ut in ordine cunctae
en: that the varied birds, all of them in their order,

latin: ostendant maculas generalis corpore inesse,
en: show the markings of their kind upon their bodies,

latin: inmutabilis materiae quoque corpus habere
en: they must surely also have a body of unchangeable

latin: debent ni mirum; nam si primordia rerum
en: matter; for if the first-beginnings of things

latin: commutari aliqua possent ratione revicta,
en: could be overcome in some way and be changed,

latin: incertum quoque iam constet quid possit oriri,
en: it would then be uncertain, too, what can come to be

latin: quid nequeat, finita potestas denique cuique
en: and what cannot, and how at last each thing's power is bounded,

latin: qua nam sit ratione atque alte terminus haerens,
en: by what principle, and its boundary-stone set deep,

latin: nec totiens possent generatim saecla referre
en: nor could the generations, kind by kind, so often repeat

latin: naturam mores victum motusque parentum.
en: the nature, the manners, the diet, and the movements of their parents.

latin: Tum porro quoniam est extremum quodque cacumen
en: Then further, since there is in each case an outermost point

latin: corporis illius, quod nostri cernere sensus
en: of that body which our senses can no longer

latin: iam nequeunt, id ni mirum sine partibus extat
en: make out, that point, beyond doubt, stands without parts

latin: et minima constat natura nec fuit umquam
en: and consists of a least nature, and was never

latin: per se secretum neque post hac esse valebit,
en: separate by itself, nor will it have the power to be hereafter,

latin: alterius quoniamst ipsum pars primaque et una,
en: since it is itself a part of another, the first and single part;

latin: inde aliae atque aliae similes ex ordine partes
en: then other parts and others, alike, in their order,

latin: agmine condenso naturam corporis explent;
en: in close-packed column fill out the nature of the body;

latin: quae quoniam per se nequeunt constare, necessest
en: and since these cannot stand by themselves, they must

latin: haerere unde queant nulla ratione revelli.
en: cling where they can by no means be torn away.

latin: sunt igitur solida primordia simplicitate,
en: The first-beginnings, therefore, are of solid singleness,

latin: quae minimis stipata cohaerent partibus arte.
en: and they cohere tightly, packed with least parts,

latin: non ex illorum conventu conciliata,
en: not combined out of a gathering of those parts,

latin: sed magis aeterna pollentia simplicitate,
en: but rather strong in eternal singleness;

latin: unde neque avelli quicquam neque deminui iam
en: from them nothing can be torn away, nothing now diminished,

latin: concedit natura reservans semina rebus.
en: so nature allows, keeping them in reserve as seeds for things.

latin: Praeterea nisi erit minimum, parvissima quaeque
en: Further, unless there is a least, the very smallest

latin: corpora constabunt ex partibus infinitis,
en: bodies will consist of infinite parts,

latin: quippe ubi dimidiae partis pars semper habebit
en: since indeed the half of a half will always have

latin: dimidiam partem nec res praefiniet ulla.
en: its own half, and nothing will set a limit.

latin: ergo rerum inter summam minimamque quod escit,
en: Therefore between the sum of things and the least of things

latin: nil erit ut distet; nam quamvis funditus omnis
en: there will be nothing to tell them apart; for however utterly

latin: summa sit infinita, tamen, parvissima quae sunt,
en: infinite the whole sum may be, still the smallest things there are

latin: ex infinitis constabunt partibus aeque.
en: will consist of infinite parts just the same.

latin: quod quoniam ratio reclamat vera negatque
en: And since true reasoning cries out against this and denies

latin: credere posse animum, victus fateare necessest
en: that the mind can believe it, you must yield and admit

latin: esse ea quae nullis iam praedita partibus extent
en: that there are things which stand endowed with no parts now

latin: et minima constent natura. quae quoniam sunt,
en: and consist of a least nature. And since these exist,

latin: illa quoque esse tibi solida atque aeterna fatendum.
en: you must admit that those, too, are solid and eternal.

latin: Denique si minimas in partis cuncta resolvi
en: Finally, if to break all things up into least parts

latin: cogere consuesset rerum natura creatrix,
en: had been the custom of the nature of things, the creator,

latin: iam nihil ex illis eadem reparare valeret
en: that same nature could restore nothing from them now,

latin: propterea quia, quae nullis sunt partibus aucta,
en: because what is furnished with no parts

latin: non possunt ea quae debet genitalis habere
en: cannot have the things that generative matter

latin: materies, varios conexus pondera plagas
en: must have: various connections, weights, blows,

latin: concursus motus, per quas res quaeque geruntur.
en: collisions, motions, by which each thing is carried on.

latin: Quapropter qui materiem rerum esse putarunt
en: Therefore those who have thought that the matter of things is

latin: ignem atque ex igni summam consistere solo,
en: fire, and that the sum of things consists of fire alone,

latin: magno opere a vera lapsi ratione videntur.
en: seem to have slipped greatly from true reasoning.

latin: Heraclitus init quorum dux proelia primus,
en: Their leader, Heraclitus, is the first to enter the battle,

latin: clarus ob obscuram linguam magis inter inanis
en: bright in fame for his dark speech, more among the empty-headed

latin: quamde gravis inter Graios, qui vera requirunt;
en: than among the serious Greeks who seek the truth;

latin: omnia enim stolidi magis admirantur amantque,
en: for fools admire and love above all those things

latin: inversis quae sub verbis latitantia cernunt,
en: which they see lurking under twisted words,

latin: veraque constituunt quae belle tangere possunt
en: and they set up as true whatever can prettily touch

latin: auris et lepido quae sunt fucata sonore.
en: the ears and is painted over with a charming sound.

latin: Nam cur tam variae res possent esse, requiro,
en: For why should things be so various, I ask,

latin: ex uno si sunt igni puroque creatae?
en: if they are created out of fire, one and pure?

latin: nil prodesset enim calidum denserier ignem
en: For it would avail nothing for hot fire to be made dense

latin: nec rare fieri, si partes ignis eandem
en: or made rare, if the parts of fire had the same

latin: naturam quam totus habet super ignis haberent.
en: nature which fire as a whole has as well.

latin: acrior ardor enim conductis partibus esset,
en: For the heat would be fiercer with its parts drawn together,

latin: languidior porro disiectis disque supatis.
en: and fainter, again, with them scattered and thrown apart.

latin: amplius hoc fieri nihil est quod posse rearis
en: More than this there is nothing you might suppose could happen

latin: talibus in causis, ne dum variantia rerum
en: under such conditions, far less that so great a variety

latin: tanta queat densis rarisque ex ignibus esse.
en: of things could arise from fires made dense and rare.

latin: Id quoque: si faciant admixtum rebus inane,
en: This too: if they were to grant void mixed in with things,

latin: denseri poterunt ignes rarique relinqui;
en: fires could be made dense and be left rare;

latin: sed quia multa sibi cernunt contraria quae sint
en: but because they see many things that would run against them

latin: et fugitant in rebus inane relinquere purum,
en: and shrink from leaving pure void in things,

latin: ardua dum metuunt, amittunt vera viai
en: while they fear the steep way, they lose the true road,

latin: nec rursum cernunt exempto rebus inane
en: nor again do they see that, with void taken from things,

latin: omnia denseri fierique ex omnibus unum
en: all things are made dense, and out of all things one

latin: corpus, nil ab se quod possit mittere raptim,
en: body is made, which could send nothing swiftly from itself,

latin: aestifer ignis uti lumen iacit atque vaporem,
en: as heat-bringing fire throws out light and warmth,

latin: ut videas non e stipatis partibus esse.
en: so that you may see it is not made of close-packed parts.

latin: Quod si forte alia credunt ratione potesse
en: But if perhaps they believe that by some other principle

latin: ignis in coetu stingui mutareque corpus,
en: fires can be quenched in combining and change their body,

latin: scilicet ex nulla facere id si parte reparcent,
en: if, that is, they will not in any part hold back from doing this,

latin: occidet ad nihilum ni mirum funditus ardor
en: then beyond doubt the heat will perish utterly into nothing,

latin: omnis et e nihilo fient quae cumque creantur;
en: all of it, and from nothing will come whatever is created;

latin: nam quod cumque suis mutatum finibus exit,
en: for whatever is changed and passes out of its own bounds,

latin: continuo hoc mors est illius quod fuit ante.
en: this at once is the death of what it was before.

latin: proinde aliquid superare necesse est incolume ollis,
en: Therefore something must survive in them unharmed,

latin: ne tibi res redeant ad nilum funditus omnes
en: so that all things do not return utterly to nothing for you,

latin: de nihiloque renata vigescat copia rerum.
en: and the store of things, reborn from nothing, grow strong.

latin: Nunc igitur quoniam certissima corpora quaedam
en: Now then, since there are certain bodies, utterly sure,

latin: sunt, quae conservant naturam semper eandem,
en: which keep their nature always the same,

latin: quorum abitu aut aditu mutatoque ordine mutant
en: by whose going away or coming in and change of order

latin: naturam res et convertunt corpora sese,
en: things change their nature and bodies are transformed,

latin: scire licet non esse haec ignea corpora rerum.
en: you may know that these bodies of things are not of fire.

latin: nil referret enim quaedam decedere, abire
en: For it would make no difference for some to withdraw and go away

latin: atque alia adtribui mutarique ordine quaedam,
en: and others to be added, and some to change their order,

latin: si tamen ardoris naturam cuncta tenerent;
en: if all of them still kept the nature of heat;

latin: ignis enim foret omnimodis quod cumque crearet.
en: for whatever they created would in every way be fire.

latin: verum, ut opinor, itast: sunt quaedam corpora, quorum
en: But in truth, as I think, it is so: there are certain bodies whose

latin: concursus motus ordo positura figurae
en: collisions, motions, order, position, shapes

latin: efficiunt ignis mutatoque ordine mutant
en: make fires, and, their order changed, change

latin: naturam neque sunt igni simulata neque ulli
en: their nature, and they are not like fire, nor like any

latin: praeterea rei quae corpora mittere possit
en: other thing which could send bodies

latin: sensibus et nostros adiectu tangere tactus.
en: to the senses and by contact touch our touch.

latin: dicere porro ignem res omnis esse neque ullam
en: Further, to say that all things are fire, and that no

latin: rem veram in numero rerum constare nisi ignem,
en: true thing exists in the number of things except fire,

latin: quod facit hic idem, perdelirum esse videtur.
en: as this same man does, seems utter madness.

latin: nam contra sensus ab sensibus ipse repugnat
en: For he himself, starting from the senses, fights against the senses

latin: et labefactat eos, unde omnia credita pendent,

en: Nor does it escape my mind how dark these things are; but with a sharp

en: thyrsus the great hope of praise has struck my heart

latin: et simul incussit suavem mi in pectus amorem
en: and at the same time has driven into my breast sweet love

latin: Musarum, quo nunc instinctus mente vigenti
en: of the Muses, inspired by which now, with vigorous mind,

latin: avia Pieridum peragro loca nullius ante
en: I range through the pathless places of the Pierides, trodden before

latin: trita solo. iuvat integros accedere fontis
en: by no one's foot. It is a joy to come to untouched springs

latin: atque haurire iuvatque novos decerpere flores
en: and drink from them, a joy to pluck new flowers

latin: insignemque meo capiti petere inde coronam,
en: and to seek for my head a crown of distinction from there

latin: unde prius nulli velarint tempora Musae;
en: where the Muses have veiled no one's temples before;

latin: primum quod magnis doceo de rebus et artis
en: first because I teach of great things, and go on

latin: religionum animum nodis exsolvere pergo,
en: to free the mind from the tight-tied knots of religion,

latin: deinde quod obscura de re tam lucida pango
en: then because on a dark matter I compose such lucid

latin: carmina musaeo contingens cuncta lepore.
en: verses, touching all of it with the Muses' charm.

latin: id quoque enim non ab nulla ratione videtur;
en: For this too seems not to be without good reason;

latin: sed vel uti pueris absinthia taetra medentes
en: but just as physicians, with foul wormwood for children,

latin: cum dare conantur, prius oras pocula circum
en: when they try to give it, first touch the rims round the cups

latin: contingunt mellis dulci flavoque liquore,
en: with the sweet and golden liquid of honey,

latin: ut puerorum aetas inprovida ludificetur
en: so that the unforeseeing age of children may be fooled

latin: labrorum tenus, interea perpotet amarum
en: as far as the lips, and meanwhile drink down the bitter

latin: absinthi laticem deceptaque non capiatur,
en: juice of wormwood, and, deceived, may not be undone,

latin: sed potius tali facto recreata valescat,
en: but rather, restored by such means, may grow strong,

latin: sic ego nunc, quoniam haec ratio plerumque videtur
en: so I now, since this reasoning often seems

latin: tristior esse quibus non est tractata, retroque
en: rather grim to those who have not handled it, and the crowd

latin: volgus abhorret ab hac, volui tibi suaviloquenti
en: shrinks back from it, have wished, in sweet-speaking

latin: carmine Pierio rationem exponere nostram
en: Pierian song, to set out for you our reasoning

latin: et quasi musaeo dulci contingere melle,
en: and, as it were, to touch it with the Muses' sweet honey,

latin: si tibi forte animum tali ratione tenere
en: if by such means I might perhaps hold your mind

latin: versibus in nostris possem, dum perspicis omnem
en: on our verses, while you see deep into the whole

latin: naturam rerum, qua constet compta figura.
en: nature of things, the shape in which it stands composed.

latin: Sed quoniam docui solidissima materiai
en: But since I have taught that the most solid bodies of matter

latin: corpora perpetuo volitare invicta per aevom,
en: fly about, unconquered, forever through the ages,

latin: nunc age, summai quaedam sit finis eorum
en: come now, whether there is some limit to their sum

latin: necne sit, evolvamus; item quod inane repertumst
en: or not, let us unfold; likewise, what has been found to be void,

latin: seu locus ac spatium, res in quo quaeque gerantur,
en: or place and space, in which all things are carried on,

latin: pervideamus utrum finitum funditus omne
en: let us see clearly whether the whole of it is bounded utterly

latin: constet an immensum pateat vasteque profundum.
en: or lies open, immeasurable and vast and deep.

latin: Omne quod est igitur nulla regione viarum
en: All that exists, then, is bounded along none of its ways;

latin: finitumst; namque extremum debebat habere.
en: for then it would have to have an outermost point.

latin: extremum porro nullius posse videtur
en: Further, it seems that nothing can have an outermost point

latin: esse, nisi ultra sit quod finiat, ut videatur
en: unless there is something beyond to bound it, so that there seems to be

latin: quo non longius haec sensus natura sequatur.
en: a point past which the nature of our sense cannot follow.

latin: nunc extra summam quoniam nihil esse fatendum,
en: As it is, since we must admit there is nothing outside the sum,

latin: non habet extremum, caret ergo fine modoque.
en: it has no outermost point; it lacks, therefore, end and measure.

latin: nec refert quibus adsistas regionibus eius;
en: Nor does it matter in which of its regions you stand;

latin: usque adeo, quem quisque locum possedit, in omnis
en: so true it is that, whatever place each one takes, on all

latin: tantundem partis infinitum omne relinquit.
en: sides alike one leaves the whole as infinite as before.

latin: Praeterea si iam finitum constituatur
en: Further, if now we should set down as bounded

latin: omne quod est spatium, si quis procurrat ad oras
en: all the space that exists, if someone should run out to its shores,

latin: ultimus extremas iaciatque volatile telum,
en: last of all, at the very edge, and hurl a flying spear,

latin: id validis utrum contortum viribus ire
en: would you rather that, whirled by strong force,

latin: quo fuerit missum mavis longeque volare,
en: it goes where it was sent and flies far off,

latin: an prohibere aliquid censes obstareque posse?
en: or do you judge that something can stop it and stand in its way?

latin: alterutrum fatearis enim sumasque necessest.
en: For you must admit and adopt one or the other.

latin: quorum utrumque tibi effugium praecludit et omne
en: Either one shuts off your escape, and forces you to grant

latin: cogit ut exempta concedas fine patere.
en: that the whole, exempt from any end, lies open.

latin: nam sive est aliquid quod probeat efficiatque
en: For whether there is something that blocks it and brings it about

latin: quo minus quo missum est veniat finique locet se,
en: that it does not reach where it was sent and lodge itself at its end,

latin: sive foras fertur, non est a fine profectum.
en: or whether it is carried on outside, it has not set out from the end.

latin: hoc pacto sequar atque, oras ubi cumque locaris
en: In this way I will follow, and, wherever you place

latin: extremas, quaeram: quid telo denique fiet?
en: the outermost shores, I will ask: what in the end becomes of the spear?

latin: fiet uti nusquam possit consistere finis
en: It will come about that no end can stand anywhere,

latin: effugiumque fugae prolatet copia semper.
en: and the scope for flight will always draw out the escape.

latin: Praeterea spatium summai totius omne
en: Further, if all the space of the whole sum

latin: undique si inclusum certis consisteret oris
en: were shut in on every side and stood within fixed shores

latin: finitumque foret, iam copia materiai
en: and were bounded, by now the store of matter

latin: undique ponderibus solidis confluxet ad imum
en: would, by its solid weights, have flowed from all sides to the bottom,

latin: nec res ulla geri sub caeli tegmine posset
en: nor could anything be carried on beneath the canopy of the sky,

latin: nec foret omnino caelum neque lumina solis,
en: nor would there be a sky at all, nor the light of the sun,

latin: quippe ubi materies omnis cumulata iaceret
en: since all matter would lie heaped up,

latin: ex infinito iam tempore subsidendo.
en: settling down from infinite time already past.

latin: at nunc ni mirum requies data principiorum
en: But as it is, plainly, no rest is given to the bodies

latin: corporibus nullast, quia nil est funditus imum,
en: of the beginnings, because there is no bottom at all

latin: quo quasi confluere et sedes ubi ponere possint.
en: where they might, as it were, flow together and take up their seats.

latin: semper in adsiduo motu res quaeque geruntur
en: Always, in ceaseless motion, all things are carried on

latin: partibus in cunctis, infernaque suppeditantur
en: in every part, and from beneath are furnished,

latin: ex infinito cita corpora materiai.
en: out of the infinite, the swift bodies of matter.

latin: Postremo ante oculos res rem finire videtur;
en: Finally, before our eyes one thing is seen to bound another;

latin: aer dissaepit collis atque aera montes,
en: air walls off the hills, and mountains the air,

latin: terra mare et contra mare terras terminat omnis;
en: land bounds the sea, and the sea in turn bounds all lands;

latin: omne quidem vero nihil est quod finiat extra.
en: but the whole, indeed, there is nothing outside to bound.

latin: est igitur natura loci spatiumque profundi,
en: There is, therefore, a nature of place and a space of the deep

latin: quod neque clara suo percurrere fulmina cursu
en: such that bright thunderbolts could not run through it in their course,

latin: perpetuo possint aevi labentia tractu
en: gliding on through an everlasting tract of age,

latin: nec prorsum facere ut restet minus ire meando;
en: nor bring it about, by going, that any less remains to go;

latin: usque adeo passim patet ingens copia rebus
en: so widely everywhere lies open a huge room for things,

latin: finibus exemptis in cunctas undique partis.
en: its boundaries taken away, in every direction on all sides.

latin: Ipsa modum porro sibi rerum summa parare
en: Further, nature prevents the sum of things itself from being able

latin: ne possit, natura tenet, quae corpus inane
en: to provide itself a limit, since she compels body to be bounded

latin: et quod inane autem est finiri corpore cogit,
en: by void, and what is void, in turn, to be bounded by body,

latin: ut sic alternis infinita omnia reddat,
en: so that by this alternation she renders the whole infinite;

latin: aut etiam alterutrum, nisi terminet alterum eorum,
en: or else, too, if the other did not bound it, one of the two

latin: simplice natura pateat tamen inmoderatum,
en: would still stretch out without measure in its single nature,

latin: nec mare nec tellus neque caeli lucida templa
en: and neither sea nor earth nor the shining precincts of heaven

latin: nec mortale genus nec divum corpora sancta
en: nor the mortal race nor the holy bodies of the gods

latin: exiguum possent horai sistere tempus;
en: could hold their ground for the brief space of an hour;

latin: nam dispulsa suo de coetu materiai
en: for, driven apart from its union, the store of matter

latin: copia ferretur magnum per inane soluta,
en: would be carried, set loose, through the great void,

latin: sive adeo potius numquam concreta creasset
en: or rather it would never have come together and created

latin: ullam rem, quoniam cogi disiecta nequisset.
en: anything, since, scattered, it could not have been driven together.

latin: nam certe neque consilio primordia rerum
en: For certainly the first-beginnings of things did not by design

latin: ordine se suo quaeque sagaci mente locarunt
en: set themselves each in its order with a shrewd mind,

latin: nec quos quaeque darent motus pepigere profecto
en: nor, surely, did they bargain what motions each should give;

latin: sed quia multa modis multis mutata per omne
en: but because, many and changed in many ways, throughout the whole

latin: ex infinito vexantur percita plagis,
en: they are harried from infinite time, struck on by blows,

latin: omne genus motus et coetus experiundo
en: by trying every kind of motion and union

latin: tandem deveniunt in talis disposituras,
en: they come at last into such arrangements

latin: qualibus haec rerum consistit summa creata,
en: as those by which this sum of things has been created and stands,

latin: et multos etiam magnos servata per annos
en: and, preserved as well through many great years

latin: ut semel in motus coniectast convenientis,
en: once it has been cast into fitting motions,

latin: efficit ut largis avidum mare fluminis undis
en: it brings about that the rivers replenish the greedy sea

latin: integrent amnes et solis terra vapore
en: with the large waves of their stream, and that the earth, warmed

latin: fota novet fetus summissaque gens animantum
en: by the sun's heat, renews her young, and the race of living things,

latin: floreat et vivant labentis aetheris ignes.
en: sent up, flourishes, and the fires of the gliding ether live.

latin: quod nullo facerent pacto, nisi materiai
en: This they could by no means do unless a store of matter

latin: ex infinito suboriri copia posset,
en: could rise up from the infinite,

latin: unde amissa solent reparare in tempore quaeque.
en: from which they are used to making good, in time, each thing lost.

latin: nam vel uti privata cibo natura animantum
en: For just as the nature of living things, robbed of food,

latin: diffluit amittens corpus, sic omnia debent
en: wastes away, losing its body, so all things must

latin: dissolui simul ac defecit suppeditare
en: dissolve as soon as matter has failed to come in supply,

latin: materies aliqua ratione aversa viai.
en: turned away by some cause from its road.

latin: nec plagae possunt extrinsecus undique summam
en: Nor can blows from outside, from every side, preserve

latin: conservare omnem, quae cumque est conciliata.
en: the whole sum, whatever has been gathered into union.

latin: cudere enim crebro possunt partemque morari,
en: For they can strike often and hold back a part

latin: dum veniant aliae ac suppleri summa queatur;
en: until others come and the sum can be filled up;

latin: inter dum resilire tamen coguntur et una
en: yet at times they are forced to rebound, and at the same time

latin: principiis rerum spatium tempusque fugai
en: to grant the beginnings of things space and time for flight,

latin: largiri, ut possint a coetu libera ferri.
en: so that they can be carried away, free from the union.

latin: quare etiam atque etiam suboriri multa necessest,
en: Therefore, again and again, many must rise up;

latin: et tamen ut plagae quoque possint suppetere ipsae,
en: and yet, so that even the blows themselves can be in supply,

latin: infinita opus est vis undique materiai.
en: there is need of an infinite force of matter on every side.

latin: Illud in his rebus longe fuge credere, Memmi,
en: In these matters, Memmius, flee far from believing

latin: in medium summae quod dicunt omnia niti
en: what they say: that all things press toward the middle of the sum,

latin: atque ideo mundi naturam stare sine ullis
en: and that for this reason the nature of the world stands without any

latin: ictibus externis neque quoquam posse resolvi
en: blows from outside, and top and bottom cannot be loosed

latin: summa atque ima, quod in medium sint omnia nixa,
en: in any direction, because all things have pressed toward the middle

latin: ipsum si quicquam posse in se sistere credis,
en: (if you believe that anything can stand upon itself),

latin: et quae pondera sunt sub terris omnia sursum
en: and that the heavy things beneath the earth all press

latin: nitier in terraque retro requiescere posta,
en: upward and rest against the earth, set there upside down,

latin: ut per aquas quae nunc rerum simulacra videmus;
en: like the images of things we now see through water;

latin: et simili ratione animalia suppa vagari
en: and contend by like reasoning that creatures wander upside down

latin: contendunt neque posse e terris in loca caeli
en: and cannot fall back out of the earth into the regions of the sky

latin: reccidere inferiora magis quam corpora nostra
en: below, any more than our bodies could

latin: sponte sua possint in caeli templa volare;
en: of their own accord fly up into the precincts of heaven;

latin: illi cum videant solem, nos sidera noctis
en: that when they see the sun, we behold the stars of night,

latin: cernere et alternis nobiscum tempora caeli
en: and that they share the seasons of heaven turn by turn with us

latin: dividere et noctes parilis agitare diebus.
en: and pass nights equal to our days.

latin: sed vanus stolidis haec * * *
en: But an empty . . . these things for fools . . .

latin: amplexi quod habent perv * * *
en: since they hold it embraced . . .

latin: nam medium nihil esse potest * * *
en: For there can be no middle . . .

latin: infinita; neque omnino, si iam medium sit,
en: infinite; nor in any way, even if there were a middle now,

latin: possit ibi quicquam consistere * * *
en: could anything stand still there . . .

latin: quam quavis alia longe ratione * * *
en: than by any other principle far . . .

latin: omnis enim locus ac spatium, quod inane vocamus,
en: For all place and space, which we call void,

latin: per medium, per non medium, concedere debet
en: must, through the middle and through what is not the middle, give way

latin: aeque ponderibus, motus qua cumque feruntur.
en: equally to weights, wherever their motions carry them.

latin: nec quisquam locus est, quo corpora cum venerunt,
en: Nor is there any place where bodies, once they have come there,

latin: ponderis amissa vi possint stare in inani;
en: can lose the force of weight and stand still in the void;

latin: nec quod inane autem est ulli subsistere debet,
en: nor must what is void hold up anything at all,

latin: quin, sua quod natura petit, concedere pergat.
en: but must go on giving way, as its nature seeks.

latin: haud igitur possunt tali ratione teneri
en: Things cannot, therefore, on such a principle be held

latin: res in concilium medii cuppedine victae.
en: in union, overcome by desire for the middle.

latin: Praeterea quoniam non omnia corpora fingunt
en: Further, since they imagine that not all bodies

latin: in medium niti, sed terrarum atque liquoris
en: press toward the middle, but only those of earth and liquid,

latin: umorem ponti magnasque e montibus undas,
en: the moisture of the sea and the great waters from the mountains,

latin: et quasi terreno quae corpore contineantur,
en: and those that are held, as it were, in an earthy body,

latin: at contra tenuis exponunt aeris auras
en: but on the contrary teach that the thin breezes of air

latin: et calidos simul a medio differrier ignis,
en: and hot fires together are carried away from the middle,

latin: atque ideo totum circum tremere aethera signis
en: and that for this reason the whole ether flickers with stars all round

latin: et solis flammam per caeli caerula pasci,
en: and the flame of the sun is fed through the blue of heaven,

latin: quod calor a medio fugiens se ibi conligat omnis,
en: because heat, fleeing from the middle, gathers all of itself there,

latin: nec prorsum arboribus summos frondescere ramos
en: and that the topmost boughs of trees could not put forth leaves at all

latin: posse, nisi a terris paulatim cuique cibatum
en: unless from the earth, little by little, food for each . . .

latin: ne volucri ritu flammarum moenia mundi
en: lest, in the manner of winged flames, the walls of the world

latin: diffugiant subito magnum per inane soluta
en: should suddenly fly apart, set loose through the great void,

latin: et ne cetera consimili ratione sequantur
en: and lest the rest should follow on a like principle,

latin: neve ruant caeli tonitralia templa superne
en: or the thundering precincts of heaven rush down from above,

latin: terraque se pedibus raptim subducat et omnis
en: and the earth swiftly slip from under our feet, and all of it,

latin: inter permixtas rerum caelique ruinas
en: amid the mingled ruins of things and of heaven,

latin: corpora solventes abeat per inane profundum,
en: that set bodies loose, pass away through the deep void,

latin: temporis ut puncto nihil extet reliquiarum
en: so that in a moment of time nothing would be left of the remnants

latin: desertum praeter spatium et primordia caeca.
en: but deserted space and unseen first-beginnings.

latin: nam qua cumque prius de parti corpora desse
en: For on whatever side you first decide that bodies

latin: constitues, haec rebus erit pars ianua leti,
en: are lacking, this side will be the door of death for things;

latin: hac se turba foras dabit omnis materiai.
en: through it the whole throng of matter will rush outward.

latin: Haec sic pernosces parva perductus opella;
en: These things you will learn thoroughly, led on with a little labor;

latin: namque alid ex alio clarescet nec tibi caeca
en: for one thing will grow clear from another, nor will blind

latin: nox iter eripiet, quin ultima naturai
en: night snatch your road away and stop you seeing through to the farthest

latin: pervideas: ita res accendent lumina rebus.
en: reaches of nature: so things will kindle lights for things.
